html:
SMTO-AUT-0014 — The sign-in service sent SMTO an answer it couldn't use

GUID: ab56673f-2bb2-534f-9134-e08450968ed6
Slug: auth-token-response-invalid
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: auth-broker

What happened

  • When SMTO asked the service for access, its reply was incomplete, unreadable, or said your sign-in is no longer active. SMTO didn't use that reply, and you may need to sign in to that service again.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to connect this saved sign-in again. When Open authorization page (or Authorize in browser) appears, select it and finish signing in on the service's page. If the service said your sign-in is no longer active, SMTO removed it, so only a fresh sign-in restores access.
  2. Before running the task again, check whether its action already happened, for example an email in your Sent folder or a new record in the other service. SMTO stopped at the sign-in step, but repeating a send or change without checking could do it twice.
  3. If the error comes back right after you sign in, send the error details to the person who set up this service's sign-in entry in Parameter Store. A reply that SMTO can never read usually means the saved sign-in settings don't match what the service sends back.

What success looks like

  • The task gets past the sign-in step and finishes without asking you to sign in again.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO or who set up this service's sign-in. Don't paste passwords, sign-in codes or anything from a parameter's Value tab into the conversation.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The auth broker rejected an OAuth token, device-authorization or PAR response that failed validation, or token introspection reported the token as not active.

What this means

  • Token/device/PAR response fields failed validation, or introspection did not confirm the token as active. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • Token/device/PAR response fields failed validation, or introspection did not confirm the token as active.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the response-validation stage with introspection active state; malformed fields and inactive tokens require different recovery.

How to fix it

  • Compare the provider response with what auth/oauth2.py accepts: a JSON object of at most 128 KiB with token_type Bearer, a non-empty access_token, a positive finite expires_in and a scope that is a subset of the requested scopes (PAR needs a urn: request_uri and a valid expires_in; device flow needs device_code, user_code and verification_uri). For auth_introspection_failed the broker already cleared the connection to authorization_required; check the oauth2_client endpoints and allowed_scopes in Parameter Store, then reconnect with auth.connect.
  • Repair provider protocol compatibility for malformed responses; reconnect the intended account when introspection shows inactive authorization.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • The response validates and any required introspection confirms current active authorization.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
